stories.headline: South Africa: Ghanaians Pack Up and Leave As Fears Spread More Ghanaian nationals are heading home as fear spreads through migrant communities across South Africa.
stories.summary: Ghanaians are leaving South Africa due to growing fears amid anti-immigration protests. A second group departed from OR Tambo International Airport on Tuesday, accepting the Ghanaian government's offer to return home. This comes as protests continue in parts of Gauteng, KwaZulu Natal, and the Eastern Cape. Demonstrators claim illegal migrants are putting pressure on public services, prompting them to ask the South African government to address the issue. An estimated 25,000 Ghanaians live in South Africa. Hundreds gathered outside the Ghanaian embassy in Pretoria for screening and verification before planned departures. The Ghanaian government's offer has provided an exit for those seeking to escape the uncertainty and fear fueled by the protests. More Ghanaians are expected to leave as the situation continues to unfold.

stories.headline: Africa: Xenophobia - Nigeria to Commence Free Evacuation of Citizens From South Africa Nigerian officials say over 1,000 citizens have registered to be evacuated and will no longer pay for their flights.
stories.summary: Nigeria has approved five repatriation flights to evacuate over 1,000 citizens from South Africa due to a surge in xenophobic attacks and anti-immigrant protests. The evacuation, ordered by President Bola Tinubu, is expected to begin this week. The Nigerian government will provide free flights to its citizens, with over 1,000 having registered to leave South Africa. The move comes amid growing concerns over the safety of Nigerians in the country, which has experienced a fresh wave of violence targeting foreigners. The repatriation effort aims to bring home Nigerians seeking to escape the rising tensions and insecurity in South Africa, which has long been a destination for African workers. The evacuation is a response to the escalating xenophobic violence, which has forced many Nigerians to flee and resulted in business losses.

stories.headline: Somalia: Somali Commandos Target Al-Shabaab Sites in Lower Shabelle Somali special forces carried out a series of planned operations in the Lower Shabelle region, targeting locations allegedly used by the Al-Shabaab to extort mo
stories.summary: Somali special forces, the elite Danab commandos, carried out planned operations in the Lower Shabelle region, targeting Al-Shabaab locations used for extorting money from local residents. The operations, conducted in areas including Warmaxan, Tasxiille, and Shareey, disrupted a planned attack by the terrorist group. The commandos dismantled a network of illegal tax collection posts operated by Al-Shabaab militants, utilizing detailed intelligence to identify and eliminate active nodes. The operation is part of a broader federal campaign to secure Lower Shabelle, a region plagued by insurgent activity due to its strategic location and proximity to the capital. The Federal Government of Somalia remains committed to eradicating Al-Shabaab and ensuring national security, in collaboration with the Somali Armed Forces and international partners. The operation was successful, with the Somali National Army and local resistance groups gaining full control of the territory.

stories.headline: Somalia Issues Official Casualty Figures After Mogadishu Clashes Somalia's Ministry of Health and Human Services said Sunday that one person was killed and 55 others wounded during security-related incidents in Mogadishu on J
stories.summary: Somalia's Ministry of Health and Human Services reported one death and 55 injuries during security-related incidents in Mogadishu on June 3 and 4. The casualties occurred amid heavy urban warfare and clan clashes in the capital. The Ministry collected data from hospitals and health facilities across Mogadishu to determine the official casualty figures. The incidents involved forces aligned with former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed and former Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire. The Federal Government of Somalia released the preliminary statistics, which contradict a joint United Nations and international humanitarian report. The Ministry's statement aims to provide an accurate account of the casualties, with the verified figures indicating one fatality and 55 wounded individuals. The clashes are part of the ongoing Somalia 2026 crisis, which has escalated into street battles and a political impasse.

stories.headline: Apple WWDC 2026 Preview: Major Siri AI Overhaul Expected as Company Seeks AI Momentum
stories.summary: Apple's WWDC 2026 is underway, with a major overhaul of Siri expected, featuring a paid tier, integration with apps like Messages and Photos, and personalized answers. The company plans to introduce AI agent integration with the app store, allowing users to delegate tasks. New Siri features may also include the ability to select different AI model providers and improvements in iOS and macOS for new device types and multitasking. The event will also showcase operating system updates for Apple's iPhone, iPad, Mac, smartwatch, and TV set-top box. This WWDC is significant as it marks Tim Cook's last as CEO, and the company aims to close the gap with competitors and boost investor confidence with its AI advancements. The keynote presentation will introduce the new features and capabilities, giving an early look at what's to come for Apple's software and services.

stories.headline: Tim Cook gets a second bite at the AI apple
stories.summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook is focusing on the company's AI efforts in his remaining months as CEO. His previous attempts at launching AI initiatives, such as Apple Intelligence 1.0 and the first Siri, were unsuccessful. Cook has acknowledged Apple Maps as one of the biggest failures under his watch, but the company's AI endeavors have been more disappointing. Apple unveiled its AI ambitions last year, partnering with OpenAI to integrate ChatGPT into Siri, rather than developing an in-house equivalent. The move comes as the company faces scrutiny, including accusations that Cook used AI in online interactions. The partnership aims to enhance Siri's capabilities, and Cook is likely seeking to leave a positive legacy in the AI space before his departure as CEO. This effort is a significant priority for Cook in his final months.

stories.headline: Singapore launches new AI supercomputer to boost climate, healthcare research
stories.summary: Singapore has launched a new AI supercomputer, Aspire 2B, to boost research in climate and healthcare. The supercomputer, located at NTU's Innovation Centre, features the country's largest cluster of advanced graphic processing units (GPUs) from Nvidia. Around 9,000 public researchers from universities, research institutes, and government agencies will have access to the supercomputer, enabling them to build more complex models and simulations. The computing power will support research in areas such as genomics and COVID-19, combining AI to tackle the pandemic. The Aspire 2B supercomputer is expected to significantly enhance research capabilities in Singapore, driving advancements in climate and healthcare research. The launch is part of the country's efforts to leverage technology and innovation to address pressing global challenges.

stories.headline: Kakao Games Unveils First In-Game Images of Supercat's New Title, 'Dokkaebi World'
stories.summary: Kakao Games has released the first in-game images of 'Dokkaebi World,' a new MMORPG under development by Supercat. The images showcase three backgrounds: Tabaro, Gwisusa, and Gwitaek, combining 2D dot characters with 3D backgrounds. The game focuses on flexible progression, skill combinations, and guild-based cooperation. Kakao Games announced the official title 'Dokkaebi's World' on June 1, confirming the game's development and plans for a combined publishing and live-service operations approach. The company will release detailed information, including content and service schedule, step by step. A launch window has not been officially announced, but the release of in-game images marks a significant step in the game's marketing cycle. Supercat, founded in 2016, is developing the game, which is a Joseon fantasy mobile MMORPG.

stories.headline: PCU-Dasmarinas ended UB’s two-year reign by winning a 3–2 thriller to capture the UCAL Season 8 Mobile Legends: Bang Bang title
stories.summary: Philippine Christian University-Dasmariñas (PCU-D) ended the University of Batangas' two-year reign in esports by winning 3-2 in the UCAL Season 8 Mobile Legends: Bang Bang finals. The match was held at the Smart Omega Bootcamp in Marikina City. PCU-D's victory was attributed to the team's synergy and strategic execution, outsmarting the University of Batangas' team, the Brahmans. This win secured PCU-D's third league title, highlighting a strong season in multiple sports events. The event was part of the PGFlex Linoleum presents UCAL 8th Season, with PCU-D's Dolphins emerging as the new champions in the popular Mobile Legends: Bang Bang tournament. The 3-2 thriller marked a significant upset, ending the University of Batangas' dominance in the esports scene.

stories.headline: 67 Celtic FC groups oppose Keane as team manager over Israel links
stories.summary: Sixty-seven Celtic FC supporter groups have signed a statement opposing Robbie Keane's potential appointment as manager due to his previous role as head coach of Maccabi Tel Aviv. The opposition stems from Keane's tenure at the Israeli club during the ongoing Gaza conflict. The statement, coordinated by Celtic Fans for the Liberation of Palestine, reflects the strong feelings of the Celtic supporters. The groups are concerned about Keane's association with Maccabi Tel Aviv, and their opposition to his potential appointment as manager has been widely reported. The statement has garnered significant support from Celtic fans, with 67 groups endorsing it, indicating a substantial level of opposition to Keane's potential appointment. The move highlights the complexities of football and politics, particularly in relation to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

stories.headline: Three Lions bid to end six decades of hurt in the United States
stories.summary: Three lions, Cleopatra, Zorya, and Mira, were relocated from Ukraine to Africa with the help of ASI donors. Meanwhile, in the US, the Detroit Lions football team had a disappointing season, gifting a playoff spot to the Green Bay Packers due to six turnovers. The team has since provided injury updates from their 2026 offseason workouts, including a medical recap for Terrion Arnold. In a separate development, three rescued African lions from Honduras were permanently relocated to the Turpentine Creek Wildlife Refuge in Arkansas. These lions were given a new home on January 15. The relocation of lions from various countries to safe havens continues, with efforts focused on preserving the species and addressing the decline of lions in Africa.

stories.headline: NEW SCHEDULE: Every session time as WorldSBK takes on Misano! Four categories and nine races await with a new Sunday schedule to close out the weekend
stories.summary: The WorldSBK is set to take on Misano with a new Sunday schedule. Four categories will compete in nine races, promising a weekend packed with action. On Sunday, four Warm Up sessions will start at 08:55, followed by the WorldSBK Tissot Superpole Race at 11:00, an earlier time than usual. The new schedule will close out the weekend, with all session times available. The event, known as the EmiliaRomagnaWorldSBK, will feature four categories and nine races, ensuring a thrilling weekend for fans. The updated schedule is now available, allowing attendees and viewers to plan their weekend accordingly.

stories.headline: TMC leader Jahangir Khan, who contested from Falta, arrested near Nepal border
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress leader Jahangir Khan, who contested from the Falta constituency, has been arrested by the Special Task Force (STF) near the India-Nepal border. Khan had pulled out of the Falta repoll last month and was evading police. He was allegedly planning to flee to Nepal when he was apprehended. The arrest was made in connection with alleged electoral malpractices. Khan, also known as 'Pushpa', was taken into custody after being on the run for some time. The STF had been tracking his movements, leading to his arrest near the border. The case is related to the recent re-poll in the Falta Assembly constituency, from which Khan had withdrawn his candidacy.

stories.headline: Indian Railways to roll out upgraded reservation system from August
stories.summary: Indian Railways will launch an upgraded Passenger Reservation System from August, marking its biggest upgrade since 1986. The new system will bring improved booking capacity, AI-based waitlist predictions, and a smoother ticketing experience. Nearly 88% of railway ticket bookings are now made online, and the upgrade aims to enhance this digital experience. The system will offer faster ticket booking and higher system capacity. The transition to the new reservation infrastructure will begin in August, with the entire project reportedly worth around ₹1,000 crore. The upgrade is expected to transform the ticket booking process with faster transactions, AI features, and an enhanced passenger experience, benefiting millions of passengers who rely on Indian Railways for travel. The launch is a significant step in modernizing India's rail network and improving passenger services.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay orders TASMAC overhaul over alleged Rs 1,600 crore diversion of unofficial 'party fund' collections
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay has ordered a major overhaul of TASMAC, the state's liquor retail corporation, amid allegations of a Rs 1,600 crore diversion of unofficial 'party fund' collections over five years. Officials have flagged massive revenue leaks, with an estimated Rs 102 crore being diverted monthly through 'party fund' commissions. In his first Cabinet meeting, Vijay initiated a crackdown on alleged corruption and revenue leakages within TASMAC. As a result, unofficial collection systems linked to TASMAC will be scrapped, with officials informing distilleries and excise departments of the changes. The move aims to halt illegal collections and plug revenue leaks within the TASMAC liquor network. The crackdown is part of Vijay's efforts to address corruption and ensure transparency in government operations.

stories.headline: INDIA Bloc Meet Live Updates: Pointed Fingers Or Alliance Unity? All Eyes On Delhi Meeting
stories.summary: The INDIA bloc meeting is underway in Delhi, bringing together leaders from 23 opposition parties. The meeting aims to address concerns over alliance unity following recent electoral setbacks. The DMK, led by MK Stalin, has skipped the meeting, citing the Congress' move in Tamil Nadu post-elections. Other key parties, including the AAP and Congress, are attending, with Congress' Mallikarjun Kharge stressing the need for unity among alliance partners. The TMC, led by Mamata Banerjee, is also attending, amid speculation of a potential split among its MPs. Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray is attending virtually, with his party reaffirming its commitment to the INDIA alliance. The meeting seeks to iron out differences and strengthen the opposition bloc ahead of future elections. Leaders are discussing issues of misgovernance by the Centre and ways to present a united front.

stories.headline: Nepal backs bilateral path with India to resolve border row; calls for partnership unconstrained by anxieties of past
stories.summary: Nepal's government has expressed its commitment to resolving border disputes with India through bilateral talks, rather than involving third parties. The two countries have reaffirmed their intention to strengthen ties despite lingering border issues. Nepal's Foreign Minister, Shishir Khanal, stated that the new government in Kathmandu aims to "reset" relations with India, moving beyond past anxieties. India has also rejected third-party involvement in resolving the border dispute, emphasizing the use of established bilateral mechanisms. High-level talks between Indian External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and Nepalese officials have taken place, with both sides expressing a desire to deepen bilateral ties. The Nepalese government has signaled a willingness to engage with India without being constrained by past geopolitical tensions, seeking a more constructive partnership.

stories.headline: Top US Professor Warns Measles Is Her Biggest Concern Ahead Of FIFA World Cup 2026
stories.summary: A top US professor has expressed concern about the spread of measles ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Recent outbreaks of Hantavirus, Norovirus, and Ebola have validated her concerns. Measles cases are surging in Mexico, which is co-hosting the World Cup, prompting health authorities to activate alerts. The US federal agency has warned of a "high likelihood" of measles being imported into Canada during the tournament. Health agencies are warning that the World Cup could amplify the spread of measles as millions of people travel between host countries. The professor notes that measles is a tricky disease, and people may be exposed during the tournament but not show symptoms until they return home, highlighting the need for vigilance and preparedness to prevent a larger outbreak. The situation is being closely monitored by health authorities.

stories.headline: US and China engage in high-stakes diplomatic talks to ease tensions over Taiwan
stories.summary: The US and China have engaged in high-stakes diplomatic talks to ease tensions over Taiwan. Chinese President Xi Jinping stressed that the "Taiwan question" is the most important issue in China-US relations, reiterating that Taiwan independence and peace in the Taiwan Strait are irreconcilable. The US has long acknowledged China's view that Taiwan is part of its territory, but maintains strong relationships with Taipei. US President Donald Trump and Xi held talks in Beijing, covering trade, tariffs, and Iran, in addition to Taiwan. Taiwan's foreign minister said the island's government is maintaining good communication with the US, and that US policy toward Taiwan has not changed. Xi is set to visit the US this fall, with China touting the recent summit as "historical" and substantive, achieving progress on trade and economic issues.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to extend grain export deal despite ongoing conflict
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to extend a grain export deal, allowing Ukrainian grain and commodities to be shipped to world markets despite the ongoing conflict. The deal, which was initially set to expire, has been extended multiple times, with Turkey playing a key role in negotiations. Russia had previously quit the deal on July 17, 2023, but rejoined in July 2025. The agreement is crucial in averting a global food crisis, as the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine contributed to rising food costs, affecting an estimated 47 million people experiencing severe hunger. The extension of the deal is expected to increase grain supplies to the world market, potentially softening grain prices. However, the deal's success relies on Russia keeping its word, as previous attacks on Ukrainian ports have undermined the agreement's effectiveness.

stories.headline: Former PM H.D. Deve Gowda coming to end of stint in public office on June 25 His party, JD(S), does not have the numbers to get him re-elected to the Rajya Sabha.
stories.summary: Former Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's stint in public office is coming to an end on June 25. His party, the Janata Dal (Secular) or JD(S), lacks the numbers to secure his re-election to the Rajya Sabha. Deve Gowda, born on May 18, 1933, served as India's Prime Minister for nearly 11 months in 1996 as part of the United Front coalition government. He became Prime Minister after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) failed to form a government and Narasimha Rao resigned. Recently, Deve Gowda made an emotional appeal in the Rajya Sabha on February 4. The Congress has criticized the BJP-JD(S) alliance after Deve Gowda was denied an NDA ticket for the upcoming election, marking the end of his long career in public office. His term in the Rajya Sabha will expire on June 25.

stories.headline: Nehru's 2 Vs Modi's 30: What Foreign Honours Say About India's Changing Global Footprint For the BJP, the gap between Nehru's two foreign honours and PM Modi's 30 serves as a visible marker of what it describes as a more assertive and globally respe
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has received over 30 foreign honours, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru's two foreign state honours. This significant difference is seen as a marker of India's changing global footprint under the BJP government. Modi's international decorations include the Israeli Parliament's highest award, which he received during a recent address. In contrast, Nehru received only two foreign state honours during his tenure. The gap between the two leaders' foreign honours highlights the shift in India's global position, with Modi's government being described as more assertive and globally respected. As of 2026, Modi has become the most internationally decorated Indian leader, with his foreign honours reflecting India's growing strategic ties with countries like the US and Israel. Modi is also set to become India's longest continuously serving elected Prime Minister.

stories.headline: Sensex falls 500 points: 3 reasons why stock market is falling today Indian markets opened sharply lower on Monday as rising Middle East tensions, higher crude prices and global weakness hit sentiment.
stories.summary: Indian markets opened sharply lower on Monday due to rising Middle East tensions, higher crude prices, and global weakness. The Sensex fell over 700 points, while the Nifty slipped below 23,150, amid a global sell-off and oil price surge. Brent oil prices jumped more than $3 a barrel after Israel's strikes on Lebanon and reported explosions in Iran. The slide has sharpened concerns over inflation, foreign outflows, and pressure on technology stocks. Retail investors, who have invested an average of $2 billion monthly for the last five years, are also affected. The benchmark equity indices saw profit booking at higher levels, paring early gains and falling sharply from the day's high levels. The combination of global triggers has led to a significant decline in the Indian stock market.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today | Opening Bell: Why Is The Stock Market Falling Today? Sensex Tanks 800 Points, Nifty Slips Below 23,150
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a significant decline, with the Sensex plummeting over 800 points and the Nifty slipping below 23,150. This downturn is attributed to fading optimism over US-China trade negotiations and rising geopolitical tensions. Additionally, the weekly futures and options (F&O) expiry also contributed to the market's decline. The Sensex and Nifty extended their losses in afternoon trade, resulting in the worst day for the market in over two months. The decline wiped out approximately ₹7 lakh crore in investor wealth. The market's reaction is also linked to concerns over US Fed and Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) trends, further exacerbating the downturn. The sharp decline in the benchmark indices has raised concerns among investors, leading to a sell-off in the market.

stories.headline: Why is market crashing today? Sensex plunges 800 points, Nifty below 23,100. 6 factors behind bloodbath on D-Street Indian stock markets experienced a significant downturn on Monday.
stories.summary: Indian stock markets experienced a significant downturn on Monday, with the Sensex plunging 800 points and the Nifty falling below 23,100. The decline was driven by a global market crash, persistent foreign institutional investor outflows, and escalating Middle East tensions. The surge in oil prices and bond yields also contributed to the downturn. Additionally, a depreciating rupee and disappointing earnings reports played a role in the market's decline. The Sensex fell 1.01% to an intraday low of 80,332.41, while the Nifty50 dropped 1.05% to 24,629.45 levels. The market crash resulted in a loss of Rs 6 lakh crore, with pharma and IT stocks being heavily sold off. Foreign fund outflows and a sweeping set of import tariffs announced by President Trump also impacted the market. Six key factors contributed to the bloodbath on D-Street.

stories.headline: Stock Market Crash: Nifty, Sensex Down 1%, All Sectors In Red: Three Reasons Why Market Is Falling Today The broader market is also facing pressure with the Nifty Smallcap 250 falling almost 0.85%, and the Nifty Midcap 150 dropping about 0.96%.
stories.summary: The Indian stock market has plummeted, with the Nifty and Sensex down 1%. All sectors are in the red, indicating a broad-based sell-off. The Nifty Smallcap 250 has fallen 0.85%, and the Nifty Midcap 150 has dropped 0.96%, reflecting pressure on the broader market. The Sensex has crashed over 889 points to 73,759.94, while the Nifty 50 has fallen 239.1 points to 23,244.45. This decline is attributed to negative global cues, weak sentiment in the IT sector, and continued selling by foreign institutional investors. The market capitalization loss is estimated to be around Rs 10-lakh crore, with pharma and IT stocks being major contributors to the decline. The downward trend has persisted, with the Nifty50 and BSE Sensex continuing their losing streak.

stories.headline: Nvidia clinches deals with South Korean giants including SK Group to advance AI boom
stories.summary: Nvidia has secured deals with major South Korean companies, including SK Group, to advance the AI boom. The partnerships, which also involve SK Telecom and Doosan Group, aim to utilize Nvidia's technology to build AI data centers. SK Group's subsidiaries, SK Hynix and SK Telecom, have agreed to deals with Nvidia, although the value of the agreements was not disclosed. Additionally, Nvidia will cooperate with South Korean internet giant Naver and conglomerate Doosan to develop AI capabilities. The partnerships were celebrated with a dinner meeting attended by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, and other prominent business leaders. The collaborations are expected to contribute to the growth of the AI industry in South Korea, with Nvidia's technology playing a key role in the development of AI data centers.

stories.headline: Oil prices rise as Iran and Israel trade strikes in defiance of Trump
stories.summary: Oil prices rose on Monday as the Middle East conflict escalated between Iran and Israel. Israel launched airstrikes on central and western Iran in response to missile fire, while Iranian forces fired missiles at Israel. The exchange of strikes followed Israeli attacks on southern Beirut suburbs targeting Hezbollah. The escalation has disrupted global oil and gas supplies, causing oil prices to climb. Earlier, prices had dipped below $100 ahead of a speech by Trump, but his address did not provide new information on US plans to exit the conflict. The conflict has made the ceasefire appear fragile, according to analysts. The situation is being closely monitored by investors, with crude oil prices increasing in early trade on Monday. The Middle East drama has significant implications for global energy markets.

stories.headline: Subsidised ferry service dropped after failed tender process
stories.summary: Alderney's Economic Development Committee has decided not to award a subsidy for a seasonal inter-island ferry service between Alderney and Guernsey after a failed tender process. The committee undertook a procurement process to appoint a ferry provider, but none of the applicants met the required criteria. As a result, the route will remain in private hands, and passengers will face higher fares. The decision was made at the committee's meeting on June 4th, where it was concluded that awarding a subsidy to a preferred provider was not possible. The subsidised ferry service was planned to operate seasonally in 2026, but these plans have now been put on hold due to the unsuccessful tender process. Passengers will have to rely on private ferry services, which are expected to be more expensive.

stories.headline: Dong Bang Co Ltd Strengthens Global Competitiveness with Advanced Veterinary Pharmaceuticals
stories.summary: Dong Bang Co Ltd is strengthening its position in the global veterinary pharmaceutical market with high-value products. The company, founded in 1983, specializes in producing veterinary pharmaceuticals for livestock and companion animals. Its product lineup includes pet anesthetics, livestock reproductive hormones, canine probiotics, and anti-inflammatory pain relief products. These products are in high demand, particularly in Southeast Asian markets. Dong Bang Co Ltd aims to enhance its global brand recognition and expand its overseas business network through exhibitions and product launches. The company's focus on advanced veterinary pharmaceuticals is expected to boost its competitiveness in the global market, with a strong presence in the production of pharmaceuticals for cattle, pigs, poultry, and pets. This strategic move is set to further establish Dong Bang Co Ltd as a key player in the veterinary pharmaceutical industry.

stories.headline: Microsoft (MSFT) Signals Ambitions to Join the Top Tier of AI Labs
stories.summary: Microsoft unveiled its new AI coding tool at the Build conference in San Francisco, signaling its ambition to join the top tier of AI labs. The company is expanding beyond providing AI cloud infrastructure and services, with plans to roll out MAI-1-preview for certain text use cases in its Copilot AI assistant. Currently, Copilot relies on OpenAI's large language models. Microsoft has started publicly testing its MAI-1-preview model on the LMArena benchmarking platform. The move comes as the company pushes aggressively into AI-driven coding, despite recent layoffs affecting roughly 6,000 employees globally, with software engineers being the hardest hit. Microsoft's AI chief stated that the company was "set free" from OpenAI to pursue superintelligence, indicating a shift in its AI strategy. The new developments were announced at the Microsoft Build 2026 event.

stories.headline: Amid AI-led layoffs, Walmart tells employees it will improve their jobs, not replace them
stories.summary: Walmart is expanding its use of artificial intelligence across the business, reassuring its 2.1 million employees that the technology will improve their jobs, not replace them. The retail giant has intensified its AI efforts, hiring a new executive to lead AI acceleration and introducing AI tools, including OpenAI's models. Despite recent layoffs of nearly 1,000 jobs, Walmart claims AI will help employees work smarter, upgrading their roles rather than making them redundant. The company is training staff to use AI technologies, aiming to integrate them into various operations. As concerns grow over AI-driven job cuts, Walmart's approach aims to alleviate fears among its workforce, emphasizing the potential benefits of AI in enhancing job performance and efficiency. The move reflects a significant shift in Walmart's strategy, as it navigates the impact of AI on its workforce and operations.

stories.headline: Top A.I. execs urge Congress to safeguard against biological weapons
stories.summary: Top artificial intelligence executives, including Google's DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, are urging Congress to safeguard against biological threats posed by AI. They have co-signed an open letter calling for improved tracking of synthetic DNA sequences that could be used for bioweapons. The executives are joining security experts in pushing for more safeguards against potential biological threats from AI. The letter asks Congress to mandate safeguards when technology companies order DNA sequences, which could be used to develop biological weapons. This rare show of unity among AI industry rivals highlights their shared concern that their technology could be misused to create bioweapons, and they are seeking tougher protections to prevent this. The move adds to growing pressure on lawmakers to address the issue.
